newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico expects 13 pct hike in '97 airport traffic.
newsitem.headline: Mexico expects 13 pct hike in '97 airport traffic.

text.p: Mexico's state airport governing body expects airport traffic in 1997 will rise by 13 percent to 52 million passengers, the group's leader said on Friday.
Aeropuertos y Servicios Auxiliares (ASA) director general Alfredo Elias told a crowd of Spanish businessmen ASA expects to see the rise in passengers as the nation's economy recovers.

Travellers through Mexican airports fell from 53 million in 1994 to between 45 million and 46 million in the following two years after the peso was devalued and the economy sunk into its worst recession in six decades.
Elas said about 38 of the nation's 58 airport are scheduled for the auction block in the second half of the year, although the scheme for their sale has not yet been outlined.
The Cancn airport in particular is an appealing property among those on the block, he said.
"Cancn is a site with a lot of potential not just because of its tourist zone, but because it could be converted into a port of transport to Europe and South America like Miami," he said.
The tourist mecca is the second most popular of Mexico's airports, following Mexico City, which ASA expected to host 18 million passengers in 1997.
About 20 unprofitable airports in smaller towns will not be auctioned, Elas added.
Mexico's two largest airlines, Aeromxico and Mexicana de Aviacin, are operated by holding company Cintra.
